I'm all long winded on the following post, so this one point I wanted to make right on top due to it's importance. Anyone who is a hard drinker, Do Not Quite Cold Turkey. Most drugs you can just stop and the withdrawals aren't deadly, they suck, but not normally deadly. Alcohol withdrawals can kill.

 

If you are looking for a way to identify if it's a problem, there are the some questions you can ask who's yes answer could be a good indicator. Is the person hiding how much/often they drink? Has social interaction lessened and can that be connected to drinking habits/requirements? Is there continuous/repeated drinking being done at times that would be inappropriate and risk effecting livelihood/life of self or others? Are there consistent, daily instances of maintenance drinking, that is; Drinking to avoid shakes/aches/sickness, such as muscle spasms in the hands or general pain; Drinking to appear sober, not having alcohol in your system would make you seem off or drunk?

 

For me, it was somewhere between maintenance drinking and hiding how often I was drinking. I didn't seek any help until I tried to stop by myself and legitimately lacked the will to do so. I'm sure situation and environment played their part, but in the end, moderation is a testament to ones will. I was the one lacking in the fortitude to moderate myself in a way that is conducive with the rest of my life. It's not some deceased, while chemical interaction does make it more than just will, will power is the big player. It is important to know for oneself dealing with it, the issue of will in this situation, while being reflected, is not conclusive to this situation. That is to say, just because you lack the will to deal with this issue right now, does not mean you are lacking in will/determination elsewhere/in-general, or that you cannot self moderate in the future. Even more important to note, others will not care that this one pitfall doesn't equate to you being a total fuck up, they will judge you as if it is the defining characteristic of you. So, to anyone seeking help, keep it hush to anyone who is not in the close trusted circle of friends. I didn't and was later informed of just how often it was part of discussions regarding me.
